_about: The caches that lie on a battle's field (the bible's loot rows: wrecks and alien remains, the rarest a chance at a blueprint, claimed by ending a move on one, a tap showing its kind and likely contents, never the contents). Ryan, 7 November: all the loot on the field from round 1, none that close to the wall; the seam's upgrade of a cache, his idea of that day, set aside with the placeholders' seam (8 November). Three kinds, one a tier from 1, their names working names (the bible's open row on the loot's names and density). per_battle caches are seeded with the map, one in each of as many bands along the wall, in the rows from rift_gap to wall_gap short of the gate's apron, each kind by its weight at the cache's depth: weight is [at the wall's end of those rows, at the rift's end], read between by the row, so the farther from the wall a cache lies the likelier a better kind (Ryan, 8 November: "place the loot, farther away it is means more likely to spawn a higher tier cache, and don't build any seam interaction yet"). The seam does nothing to a cache. Each holds salvage [lo, hi], so many components of the battle's tier, and a blueprint chance at a component of that tier the run holds no blueprint for. Shown: name, and codex (empty until Ryan writes one; a tap's readout says the likely contents from the numbers). Every number a placeholder.
